targets.X: when g_a(x) = (a-1)x^2 + 2(a-1)x + (a-1) is the zero polynomial, its degree otherwise, and assessment of degree bound contradiction
targets.Y: zero polynomial definition (all coefficients zero) and degree bound hypothesis (applies only to non-zero polynomials)
targets.Z: all coefficients equal zero iff a = 1; when a != 1, leading coefficient (a-1) != 0 so degree is 2
targets.W: an arbitrarily large number of zeros at a = 1 does NOT contradict the degree bound because that theorem explicitly requires a non-zero polynomial
targets.wrong_idea: Thinking the degree of the zero polynomial is 0, or claiming that having infinite zeros contradicts the fundamental degree bound theorem.
targets.replacement_rule: The degree bound theorem applies strictly to non-zero polynomials; the zero polynomial has undefined degree and vanishes everywhere.
